title: Ordinary and completed tensor with an integral coefficient line
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $X$ a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. On its small pro-etale site put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $C\in D(R)$ be derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], and let $T$ be an $R$-module sheaf locally isomorphic to $R$ and placed in degree zero. Use the ordinary derived tensor $\otimes_R^L$ in $D(R)$, the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] over $R$ after K-flat replacement of the first factor [def-pc-kflat-complex], and the completed tensor $\widehat\otimes^L$ defined by the functorial reduction-tower cone construction of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Write $C_n=C\otimes_R^L(R/\varpi^n)$, $T_n=T\otimes_R(R/\varpi^n)$, and regard each finite reduction as an $R$-complex by restriction of scalars. The natural reduction maps induce an isomorphism
$$
C\otimes_R^L T\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n(C_n\otimes_{R/\varpi^n}^L T_n)=C\widehat\otimes^L T.
$$
Here the comparison is obtained on a K-flat representative $P\to C$ by the canonical map from $P\otimes_R T$ to the shifted cone of $1-s$ on the products of its reductions. It is natural in $C$ and in isomorphisms of such $T$, and its reduction at every $n$ is the ordinary tensor/reduction identification.
